question: Should Gateway origin policy allow `chrome-extension://*`, and if so should it live inside `allowedOrigins` or a constrained pattern surface?
rationale: This changes a browser-origin security boundary and the current contract says `allowedOrigins` contains full origins only; automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust grammar or acceptable extension-origin blast radius.

options.title: Approve constrained pattern policy
options.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern surface or grammar for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no ad hoc prefix matching.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Leave scheme wildcards unsupported and focus related PRs on exact non-standard-origin matching, accepting that extension ID churn remains an operator burden.

options.title: Reject extension-wide trust
options.body: Close this direction after documenting that trusting all Chrome extension origins is too broad for Gateway origin authorization.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained pattern policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern surface or grammar for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no ad hoc prefix matching.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Gateway origin hardening and non-loopback origin requirements appear to originate from steipete-authored commits, making this the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
